ceviri.14: SEO reporting is the reporting process that measures organic search performance regularly, broken down by query, page and conversion.
ceviri.16: Google Search Console is the free measurement tool that shows a site's clicks, impressions and index status in the search results.
ceviri.33: Is a paid tool essential for SEO reporting?
ceviri.34: No. The trio of Search Console, GA4 and Looker Studio is free and more than covers an SME's decision-making needs. Paid tools offer extra layers such as competitor tracking, keyword volume and link profiles. Those are useful, not essential. Set the free trio up properly first and let the data start flowing; you'll see concretely, six months on, where you feel the gap. The decision then rests on a real need. And when you do move to a paid tool, start by closing one single gap; buying a package and trying to use all of it at once just crowds the report.
ceviri.35: How long does the setup take?
ceviri.36: On our own projects, two working days with one person is enough. Tag placement and conversion definitions can be finished the same day; the real time goes into building the dashboard.
ceviri.37: Why does Search Console data come out different from GA4?
ceviri.38: The two tools count different things. Search Console measures the click in the search result, GA4 the session opened on the site. There is always a gap between them; it's enough for the gap to stay within a reasonable range.
ceviri.39: How often should we produce the report?
ceviri.40: A monthly rhythm is enough for most businesses. Do the weekly check through the dashboard and share the annotated document on the fifth of the month.
ceviri.42: Search Console doesn't provide historical data. GA4 doesn't show anything before the setup date either. That's why opening the properties today is the cheapest investment there is.
ceviri.43: Is the data lost when we change agency?
ceviri.44: Not if the properties are tied to the business's account. If ownership is in the agency's account the risk is real; keep ownership in your own corporate account and give the agency user permissions only.
ceviri.45: How many metrics should be on the dashboard?
ceviri.46: As many as fit on one screen. Eight to ten metrics cover most decisions; more than that distracts.
ceviri.47: Who should do the SEO reporting setup?
ceviri.48: The software and the marketing sides should work together. Tag placement is technical work, while defining conversions is a commercial decision.

ceviri.63: A screenshot of a ranking isn't a report on its own. The question you're asking is simple: which page earned what this month? Building the order that answers it starts with configuring the tools correctly. SEO reporting is Search Console, GA4 and an automation layer all working on the same definitions. In this piece we set out the setup order for those three layers, their critical settings, and the points that break the data when they're skipped.
ceviri.64: When Search Console, GA4 and the automation layer meet in one order, the report produces decisions.
ceviri.66: What Is SEO Reporting and What Does It Measure?
ceviri.67: SEO reporting is the measurement process that gathers visibility and click data from organic search into a single order. The measurement covers the breakdown by query, page, device and conversion. The aim isn't to present a long list of metrics. The real job is showing which page produces revenue and which one burns budget for nothing. A wrong setup makes that distinction impossible from the outset.
ceviri.68: Data is never in short supply on an agency desk; what's in short supply is decisions. A report is the document that shortens the data enough to answer a single question.
ceviri.69: The number of businesses moving to digital channels in Türkiye rises every year;
ceviri.70: the Ministry of Trade's ETBİS bulletin
ceviri.71: sets that rise out in concrete numbers — ETBİS is Türkiye's e-commerce information system. As the competition hardens, managing on guesswork gets expensive. The reporting layer becomes the single source of truth for the SEO work.
ceviri.72: Is a report the same thing as a dashboard?
ceviri.73: A dashboard carries live data, a report carries the interpretation of a period. A healthy SEO reporting order sets both up together.
ceviri.75: The number of metrics that produce decisions is small. Clicks by page, average position, the number of conversions and organic sessions per conversion close most meetings. If you want to go deeper, the audit findings on the
ceviri.77: side explain the reason behind those numbers.
ceviri.78: How Do You Set Search Console Up Correctly?
ceviri.79: Setting Search Console up starts with verification at domain level; a DNS record gathers all the subdomains into a single property. In SEO reporting terms, setting it up early is a direct gain. The accumulation of data starts on the day of setup; historical dates don't arrive later. That choice also prevents the www and non-www versions being reported separately.
ceviri.80: Postponing the setup is a direct loss of data. Search Console is the free tool that shows performance at query level. Finish the verification before you take a new site live.
ceviri.81: Once the property is open, two jobs remain. Submit the sitemap and define the user permissions. If more than one team will read the report, everyone should connect to the same property with their own permission. Distributing the permissions correctly from the start also makes changing agency easier later.
ceviri.83: DNS verification is permanent; the file method can be lost in a theme update. Adding a TXT record is finished in one sitting.
ceviri.84: What do you look at when submitting a sitemap?
ceviri.85: A sitemap lists the addresses you want in the index. The coverage report, meanwhile, tells you which page has been left out and why.
ceviri.86: One property, or a second one?
ceviri.87: The domain property is your main source. Opening a second URL-prefix property for a blog or campaign subdomain lets you see that section in isolation.
ceviri.88: Which Settings Are Essential on the GA4 Side?
ceviri.89: There are three essential settings on the GA4 side. You mark the conversion events, you filter internal traffic, and you set up the Search Console connection. Until those three are complete you can't work out what organic traffic is worth in money. The default setup only collects page views. A form submission, a phone tap and a quote request each need defining as a separate event.
ceviri.90: The setup wizard takes you quickly to the finish screen; the real work starts afterwards. GA4 is the measurement platform that records user behaviour on an event basis. When you add the tag you see the traffic; you don't see the business outcome.
ceviri.91: The second critical point is internal traffic. Exclude office IP addresses and agency access.
ceviri.93: — if that filter isn't in the table where you'll combine this with the ad data, the cost calculation inflates. Desktop and mobile visitors don't behave the same way when it comes to converting either; that's why keeping the device breakdown separate in SEO reporting is meaningful.
ceviri.95: The business draws up the list, the software team carries out the implementation. In an SEO reporting setup, that list is the only agenda item of the first meeting. Only the sales side knows which action means revenue.
ceviri.96: What does the Search Console connection open up?
ceviri.97: Once the connection is made, query and behaviour data meet on the same screen; you read which search arrived at which page in a single report.
ceviri.98: How Does the Automation Layer Take Over the Monthly Report?
ceviri.99: The automation layer combines the data from the two tools in a single dashboard and removes the burden of preparing the monthly report by hand. Looker Studio is the visualisation application that does that combining for free. The setup that feeds SEO reporting is a one-off. You define the date comparison, the segment and the target line once. All that's left afterwards is writing the commentary.
ceviri.100: A document prepared by hand neither earns its keep nor keeps the definitions fixed. An automated dashboard fixes the definitions, and the comparison then means something.
ceviri.101: A summary, a page breakdown and a conversion view are enough on most SEO reporting dashboards. On corporate projects we set that screen up within the scope of
ceviri.103: as the single source of truth we share with the client. Reporting discipline also makes visible where the SEO budget is going.
ceviri.104: How is the Looker Studio connection set up?
ceviri.105: You connect the GA4 and the Search Console property separately. Leaving the sources apart rather than producing blended metrics reduces misreading.
ceviri.106: Do you need to archive the raw data?
ceviri.107: You do. Interfaces put a limit on dates; the table you export doesn't. Downloading the monthly raw data into a spreadsheet lets you compare seasonality two years later.

ceviri.110: How Do Setup Mistakes Break the Report?
ceviri.111: Setup mistakes break a report quietly; the screen looks like it's working but the numbers don't tell the truth. Unfiltered internal traffic, a duplicate tag, a missing subdomain property and the wrong time zone are the four most common mistakes. All four shift the monthly curve. Until an audit is done, none of them shows itself.
ceviri.112: A tag that fires twice makes the session and conversion counts look higher than they are. Theme updates are the most common source; the template adds the measurement code a second time.
ceviri.113: A missing subdomain property works the other way. When a subdomain doesn't fall under the main property, the clicks from that section don't appear in the report. Before you close an SEO reporting setup, go through the subdomain list one by one. The time zone is a silent mistake too; if GA4 and the dashboard are on different zones, the month-end doesn't tally.
ceviri.114: Why should internal traffic be filtered?
ceviri.115: Checks made from the office imitate real demand and inflate the total on small sites. Once the filter comes into play, the number that drops is the correct one.
ceviri.116: How do you reflect the data lag in the report?
ceviri.117: Search Console data completes with a lag of a few days. A document you pull on the first of the month shows the last days short. Moving the schedule to the fifth largely closes that deviation.
ceviri.118: The SEO Reporting Order: A Six-Step Tool Setup List
ceviri.119: Verification comes first, then measurement, and automation last. When you build the SEO reporting order in that sequence, your report fills itself by the end of the six steps. On our own projects the workload doesn't exceed two working days with one person. None of the steps asks for a paid tool; the free layer is more than enough to start with.
ceviri.121: Open the Search Console property with a DNS record and gather the subdomains under one roof.
ceviri.123: Submit the live addresses and read the coverage report in the first week.
ceviri.125: Place the tag from a single point and finish the duplicate-firing check the same day.
ceviri.127: Mark the form, the phone call and the quote request each as an event.
ceviri.129: Exclude office and agency IP addresses, and fix the zone to a single value.
ceviri.131: Combine the two sources in Looker Studio and share the document on the fifth of the month.
ceviri.132: You can carry this list out with your own team. If you'd like to hand the SEO reporting setup over to us, write through

ceviri.135: What should you look at in the first 30 days?
ceviri.136: Don't expect rankings in the first month. The only thing to look at is the integrity of the data. Are the conversion events landing, is there an unexpected error in the coverage report? The first gain is correct measurement itself.
ceviri.137: Correctly configured settings align the numbers in the monthly report with reality.

ceviri.165: Let's work out the route map that suits your scope together; let's settle the steps and the timing.
ceviri.168: The measurement setup is the ground under every decision on the search side. When the tools are connected correctly, the discussion moves on from “have the rankings dropped” to “which page should we put budget behind”. A habit of regular SEO reporting leaves you with a comparable history six months later. Without that history you can't prove your claim to growth.
